Test Description: Verify that the public homepage opens successfully and exposes its primary page content and Login navigation.
Preconditions: Apache is running; the application is available at http://localhost/barbershop-1/; no authenticated session is active.
Test Steps: 1. Open the application URL; 2. Verify the navigation response is successful; 3. Verify the page body is visible; 4. Verify the Login link is visible.
Expected Result: The server returns a successful HTTP response, the page body is visible, and the Login link is visible.
Actual Result: Codex-verified Chromium execution passed all assertions. Test duration: 3.7 seconds; overall one-test run: 6.5 seconds.
Remarks: Separate historical result: the user reported a successful Chromium run of approximately 1.5 seconds on the same date.

Test Description: Verify that a registered regular user can sign in with valid credentials.
Preconditions: Apache and MySQL are running; the application database is available; a dedicated non-sensitive QA user exists; the user is logged out.
Test Steps: 1. Open login.php; 2. Enter the QA user's Email Address; 3. Enter the QA user's Password; 4. Select Login; 5. Verify successful authentication and expected destination.
Test Data: Dedicated QA account supplied through secure local test data; never commit its password.
Expected Result: The user is authenticated and redirected to index.php, or to the originally requested page when a redirect was stored; authenticated profile controls replace the Login link.
Remarks: Planned test. No credentials are stored in this repository.

Test Description: Verify that authentication is rejected when a syntactically valid but unregistered credential pair is submitted.
Preconditions: Apache and MySQL are running; the application database is available; the user is logged out.
Test Steps: 1. Open login.php; 2. Enter a syntactically valid unregistered email; 3. Enter an incorrect password; 4. Select Login; 5. Observe the response.
Test Data: Email: qa.invalid@example.test; Password: non-production placeholder supplied at runtime.
Expected Result: The user remains unauthenticated on the login page and an 'Invalid email or password' message is displayed.
Remarks: Planned test; use reserved or controlled test data only.

Test Description: Verify client-side required-field validation when the login form is submitted empty.
Preconditions: The application is available and the user is logged out.
Test Steps: 1. Open login.php; 2. Leave Email Address empty; 3. Leave Password empty; 4. Select Login; 5. Observe both fields.
Expected Result: Submission is prevented; Email Address shows 'Email address is required' and Password shows 'Password is required'.
Remarks: Planned test based on the inspected login form and client-side validation.

Test Description: Verify that a homepage product can be added to the browser cart.
Preconditions: The public homepage is available; browser local storage is cleared for an isolated run.
Test Steps: 1. Open the homepage; 2. Locate Premium Pomade; 3. Select its Add to Cart button; 4. Verify the confirmation notification; 5. Inspect the cart stored in local storage.
Test Data: Product: Premium Pomade; ID: 1; Price: 15; Quantity: 1.
Expected Result: A confirmation states that Premium Pomade was added, and local storage contains the product with quantity 1.
Remarks: Planned test. This case validates the homepage cart behavior, not checkout or payment.
